admission_process application steps step: 1. action: Visit EWU admission website. details: Go to http://www.ewubd.edu or directly to http://admission.ewubd.edu
admission_process application steps step: 2. action: Create New Applicant. details: Click 'Create New Applicant' and select desired program. Program cannot be changed later.
admission_process application steps step: 3. action: Enter basic info. details: Fill in Name, Mobile Number, Email (optional). A unique 'EWU Login ID' will be generated and shown on the next screen.
admission_process application steps step: 4. action: Note EWU Login ID. details: Example: 163354131. Required for payment and login. Also sent via email. Pay slip can be downloaded/printed.
admission_process application steps step: 6. action: Sign In. details: Use EWU Login ID and Mobile Number to sign in after payment clearance.
admission_process application steps details uploads_required photo description: Recent passport size color photo. format: jpg. max size: 100Kb. dimensions: 240x300 pixels
admission_process application steps details uploads_required signature description: Scanned signature on white background. format: jpg. max size: 60Kb. dimensions: 300x80 pixels

admission_process application steps step: 9. action: Receive Confirmation. details: After successful submission, a confirmation message appears: 'Your form has been submitted successfully. For obtaining the Admit Card click on the Admit Card'.

admission_requirements undergraduate general_programs_except_bpharm o_a_levels grading_scale A: 5. B: 4. C: 3. D: 2. E: 1
admission_requirements undergraduate general_programs_except_bpharm admission_test weightage admission test: 75%. ssc o level: 10%. hsc a level: 15%

admission_requirements undergraduate general_programs_except_bpharm subject_requirements cse: Mathematics & Physics in HSC or A Level. ice: Mathematics & Physics in HSC or A Level. eee: Mathematics & Physics in HSC or A Level. geb: Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Mathematics in HSC or equivalent; Biology in SSC. civil: Mathematics, Chemistry & Physics in HSC or A Level. mathematics: Mathematics in HSC or equivalent. data science: Mathematics in HSC or equivalent
admission_requirements undergraduate bpharm ssc_hsc aggregate: Minimum GPA 8.00 (on scale of 10). minimum each: Not less than GPA 3.50 in any examination.
admission_requirements undergraduate bpharm subject_gpa chemistry: Min GPA 3.5. biology: Min GPA 3.5. physics: Min GPA 3.0. mathematics: Min GPA 3.0
admission_requirements undergraduate bpharm o_a_level_grades chemistry: Grade B. biology: Grade B. mathematics: Grade C. physics: Grade C
admission_requirements undergraduate bpharm foreign_students schooling: Must have completed 12 academic years.. equivalency: Certificate required from Pharmacy Council of Bangladesh (PCB).
admission_requirements undergraduate bpharm assessment written test: Mandatory competitive written test.. oral test: May also be taken for further assessment.

admission_requirements waivers sat_waiver requirement: Minimum total SAT score of 1500 (Critical Reading, Math, Writing).. science engineering additional: Min GPA 3.5 in Math and Physics separately in HSC/A Level.

admission_requirements foreign_students schooling: Must have 12 years of schooling.. sat: SAT score 1100 OR upper 50% marks/grade in their education system.. assessment: Equivalence committee will assess eligibility and may recommend scholarships/financial aid.

admission_requirements graduate mba_emba o_a_levels requirement: Passed O Level in at least 5 subjects and A Level in at least 2 subjects.. condition: At least 4B's (GPA 4.0) and 3C's (GPA 3.5) among the 7 subjects.
admission_requirements graduate mba_emba mba work experience: Preferred but not essential.
admission_requirements graduate mba_emba emba work experience: Minimum 2 years after graduation in executive position.. admission basis: Interview-based selection.
admission_requirements graduate mba_emba test_exemptions ewu graduates: UG CGPA ≥ 3.00 exempt from written admission test.. other universities: CGPA ≥ 3.50 exempt from written admission test.

events_workshops title: World Pharmacists Day 2025 Celebration at EWU. date: 2025-09-25. description: On 25 September 2025, the Department of Pharmacy at East West University organized a vibrant day-long program to celebrate World Pharmacists Day.

events_workshops title: East West University Welcomes Freshers for the Fall Semester 2025. date: 2025-09-25. description: East West University (EWU) welcomed approximately 1,800 newly admitted students through a comprehensive Orientation Program for the Fall Semester 2025.

events_workshops title: DCCI and EWU Sign MoC to Strengthen Industry-Academia Collaboration and Foster Entrepreneurship. date: 2025-09-08. description: The Dhaka Chamber of Commerce & Industry (DCCI) and East West University (EWU) officially signed a Memorandum of Cooperation to enhance industry-academia collaboration.

events_workshops title: Stepping into the Future: GDLFM Program Makes Strides at BLF Expo 2025. date: 2025-08-23. description: The EDC under SICIP at EWU showcased progress of the GDLFM Program at the BLF Expo 2025.

events_workshops title: East West University Advances Community Legal Literacy through the Street Law Program. date: 2025-08-21. description: Street Law initiative by EWU aims to make legal knowledge accessible to the public, especially marginalized communities.

events_workshops title: Intra-University Programming Contest - Summer 2025. date: 2025-08-11. description: The Department of CSE organized the Intra-University Programming Contest - Summer 2025 to promote problem-solving skills among students.

events_workshops title: Department of Sociology Hosts Seminar on Begum Rokeya's Sultana's Dream. date: 2025-08-10. description: The Department of Sociology hosted a seminar to celebrate Begum Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain's seminal feminist work.

events_workshops title: East West University Hosts Panel Discussion on Harnessing Information Systems for Business in Bangladesh. date: 2025-08-07. description: The Department of Business Administration organized a high-profile panel discussion on information systems for business.

events_workshops title: Teachers' Training Program on 'Teaching, Learning, and Research'. date: 2025-08-07. description: A series of training modules were conducted as part of the Teachers' Training Program at EWU.

faculty sections academic background: Ph.D in Computer Science and Engineering, Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology, Dhaka, BangladeshM.Sc Engg.  in Computer  Engineering, Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology, Dhaka, BangladeshB.Sc Engg. in Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology, Dhaka, Bangladesh. short biography: Dr. Md. Mozammel Huq Azad Khan is currently a Professor of the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at East West University, Dhaka. He is one of the pioneering professors of Computer Science and Engineering in Bangladesh.  He started his teaching career in the Electrical and Electronic Engineering Department at Bangladesh Institute of Technology (BIT), Rajshahi, which is currently known as Rajshahi University of Engineering and Technology (RUET), in 1986. In 1991 he shifted to Khulna University and, as the founder Head of the Department, established Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) Department there, which was the second of its kind in the country after that of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET), Dhaka. As founder Head, he also established Electronics and Communications Engineering (ECE) Department at Khulna University in 1997, which was the first ever ECE program in the country. He was the second Dean of Science, Engineering and Technology School at Khulna University. In 1999 he joined East West University as Professor and played an instrumental role in introducing CSE program in the then Computer Science Department and helped rename the department as Computer Science and Engineering Department. He also played a pivotal role in introducing and updating MS program in the department. In 2018, he played the key role in introducing outcome-based curriculum for B. Sc. in CSE program as required by the Board of Accreditation for Engineering and Technical Education (BAETE), Institution of Engineers, Bangladesh (IEB). The B. Sc. in CSE program of EWU is now accredited by BAETE and Washington Accord, where his contribution was enormous. He served as the Chairperson of the CSE department thrice. He is also the first Dean of the Faculty of Sciences and Engineering at East West University. He, as the founder Chairperson, established Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) Department at East West University.During September to December 2015, he served as a Visiting Scholar in the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science at the University of Lethbridge, Alberta, Canada.He served as a member of the Quality Assurance Cell of BAETE for two years.Prof. Khan has authored and co-authored numerous peer-reviewed research papers and presented works at many national and international conferences. He has published journal publications in internationally reputed, indexed, and peer-reviewed journals likeIEEE Access,VLSI Design,J. Supercomputing,IEEE Trans. VLSI,J. System Architecture,J. Multiple-Valued Logic and Soft Computing,Intl. J. Electronics,Information Processing Letters, etc. He also authored  conference papers in top rated Conferences worldwide. Prof. Khan has active research collaboration with professors of Portland State University, USA, University of Lethbridge, Canada, and University of Kentucky, USA. His most research works are in the broad field of reversible and quantum computing, where he introduced many fundamental concepts and ideas that are highly acclaimed by the global research community. His fields of research interests include Reversible/Quantum Logic, Multiple-Valued Logic, Evolutionary Algorithms, Graph Problems, Data Mining, and Machine Learning. He recently published a novel and efficient clustering algorithm. He is the author of a textbook titled "Digital Logic Design" published by the University Grants Commission (UGC) of Bangladesh.. professional experience: Teaching PositionsSept 1999 – faculty sections academic background: IFLA, ALP FellowVictoria University of Wellington, New ZealandIVLP FellowU.S. Department of State's premier professional exchange programPh.D. in Information Literacy(Punjabi University, India)MAin Library and Information Science(University of Dhaka)BA (Hon’s)in Library and Information Science(University of Dhaka)Training/workshopsCreative Commons Certificate for galleries, libraries, archives and museums (GLAMs), Creative Commons: A nonprofit organization, located in California, United States. short biography: Dr. Dilara Begumis a Professor and Chairperson, Department of Information Studies and Librarian (In-Charge) at East West University, Dhaka, Bangladesh. She was a former fellow of IFLA, ALP (Victoria University of Wellington, New Zealand). With a rich history of over 26 years in research, teaching, and information management, Dr. Begum has significantly influenced the academic and practical fields of library and information sciences. In the international arena, she has garnered recognition through numerous roles. Notably, she has been elected as aGoverning Board Member of the International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions (IFLA)for the 2023-2025 term and has served as the elected Professional Division Committee Chair-C and an Asia Oceania Regional Division Committee member of IFLA from 2021-2023.  Her influence extends to varied and pivotal roles, such as serving as General Secretary of DLNetSA and Country Coordinator of the Information Literacy Consortium sponsored by UNESCO, President (Acting) of Library Association of Bangladesh (LAB), among others. A standout accomplishment in her career is the establishment of the Department of Information Studies at East West University.Dr. Dilara has more than 80 scholarly articles in peer-reviewed journals published by renowned publishers such as Emerald Publishing Limited, SAGE Publishing, Routledge etc. She has edited a book on Knowledge Management, Governance, and Sustainable Development Lessons and Insights from Developing Countries published by Routledge; an imprint of the Taylor & Francis Group, UK. [ISBN: 9780367546281]. She is working as Regional Editor for Digital Library Perspectives Journal, indexed in Scopus; Published by Emerald Publishing Limited. She is also working as an executive editor of the International Journal of Information Studies and Knowledge Management [ISSN 2789-5920, E-ISSN 2790-3265].As an invited speaker, Dr. Begum has presented academic papers in more than sixty international and national conferences and seminars in USA, Mexico, UK, France, Spain, Netherlands, Ireland, Sweden, Norway, South Africa, Greece, Estonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Turkey, Malaysia, China, Indonesia, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, Nepal, etc. She has been awarded with the prestigious award, "Prof. Indira Parikh 50 Women in Education Leaders" on 05thJuly 2018 in Mumbai at the World Education Congress recognizing her contribution in education. Recently, she honored with the ‘Lifetime Achievement Award 2023’ by COLLNET, Society for Library Professionals (SLP) and Special Libraries Association (SLA), Asia Community for her outstanding contribution in research, collaboration, and library development for more than 25 years. In addition to her academic and organizational contributions, Dr. Begum has also been a pivotal consultant for over 30 public and private organizations, guiding them in developing their library systems. faculty sections academic background: PhD, Clarkson University, USAMS, Texas A & M University, USAMSc, BUETBSc, BUET. short biography: Dr. Anisul Haque is working as a professor in the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, East West University since 2006. He has also served as the Chairperson of the Department of EEE and the Dean of the Faculty of Sciences and Engineering. Before joining East West University, he taught at the Electrical and Electronic Engineering Department, BUET for eighteen years. He has been a visiting faculty at Tokyo Institute of Technology, Japan, University of Connecticut, USA and Clarkson University, USA. Dr. Haque’s research interests include the physics, modeling, simulation and characterization of nanoelectronic devices and photovoltaic devices and systems. He is also interested in engineering education. Dr. Haque is the recipient of the Bangladesh University Grants Commission Award in 2006 and the gold medal from the Bangladesh Academy of Science in 2010. Dr. Haque was an editor ofIEEE Transactions on Electron Devicesfrom 2010 to 2019. He also served as an associate editor ofIEEE Accessfrom 2013 to 2023. He has been serving as anIEEE Distinguished Lecturersince 2009. He is also in the Board of Accreditation for Engineering and Technical Education (BAETE), Institute of Engineers, Bangladesh (IEB) as a board member. Dr Haque has conducted many training and workshop sessions on Outcomes Based Education (OBE) for academic program leaders and on Outcomes Based Accreditation (OBA) for BAETE program evaluators.. professional experience: Professor, EEE, East West University 2006 - presentProfessor/Associate Professor/Assistant Professor/Lecturer, EEE, BUET 1987 - 2005. research interest: Photovoltaic devices and systemsModeling, simulation and characterization of semiconductor devicesEngineering education. selected publications: Journal PublicationBook chaptersM. He is a Professor in the Department of Pharmacy at East West University.After graduating with a Bachelor of Pharmacy from Dhaka University in 1987, he pursued his academic journey at the Chiba University of Japan. He obtained his Master of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Doctor of Pharmaceutical Sciences degrees in 1991 and 1994, respectively. During his doctoral studies, he made a significant discovery by identifying a series of novel small-molecule Natural-Products with selective monoamine-B inhibitory activity from a fungus,Monascas anka.Prof. Hossain was awarded a prestigious fellowship from theScience and Technology Agency (STA)of the Japanese government in 1994 and placed at theNational Institute of Health Science(NIHS) in Japan to complete his post-doctoral studies. Later in 1995, he was also awarded a Human Science Foundation post-doctoral fellowship for three years.In 1996, he embarked on a teaching career as an Assistant Professor in the Pharmacy Department at Dhaka University, later being promoted to Associate Professor in 2000.In the same year, he was invited to work as a Visiting Scientist at theNational Center for Natural Products Research (NCNPR)of theUniversity of Mississippi,USA, where he collaborated with well-renowned F.A.P. Barnard Distinguished Professor Alice M. Clark’s research group. During his tenure in the USA, Prof. Hossain made seminal contributions to federally funded anticancer research projects, pioneering the discovery and characterization of novel antitumor agents that effectively inhibit the hypoxia-inducible survival factor (HIF-1) in breast tumor cells. Dr. Hossain discovered a series of dineolignans, manassantins, from an aquatic plant asthe most potent inhibitor of HIF-1α ever known to date.Notably, he unveiled a potent series ofdineolignans, manassantins, from an aquatic plant, marking an unparalleled advancement in HIF-1α inhibitor research. His research was underscored bytwo US patentsand numerous peer-reviewed publications, with one receiving the Jack L. Beal Award by the American Society of Pharmacognosy for beingthe best manuscript published in 2004 in the flagship journal, theJournal of Natural Products.After returning from the USA, Dr. Hossain joined Manarat International University as an Associate Professor and attained the rank of Professor within a short span. In January 2009, he joined East West University as a Professor. He has since served the university in various capacities, including as the Dean of the Faculty of Sciences and Engineering, Chairperson of the Department of Pharmacy, and member of the Syndicate and the Academic Council.In recognition of his outstanding academic research contributions, he received a Certificate of Excellence from East West University in 2009. Furthermore, he was honored with the Bangladesh Education Leadership Awards in2019 for the Best Professor in Pharmacy Studies by the World Education Congress.Prof. Hossain is currently working on natural-products-based drug discovery for non- alcoholic steatohepatitis from medicinal plants of Bangladesh. Professor Rahman has advised multinational firms on issues such as remanufacturing, lean manufacturing, sustainable procurement, and talent management. He is frequently called upon to deliver keynotes and present workshops for professional bodies and senior executives. Professor Rahman has published over 250 research papers and successfully supervised 25 PhD candidates. He is an Associate Editor of the International Journal of Information Systems and Supply Chain Management andserveson the editorial board of fifteen international journals. He has been teaching at East West University since January 2006. He served as Chairman of Department of English in 2009 (January-December), Dean of Faculty of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences (FLASS), EWU, from September 2012-September 2014, and Director of Institutional Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) of East West University, from November  2015 to January 2016. He was also the Vice President of Bangladesh English Language Teachers Association (BELTA) from 2013 to 2015. Furthermore, he is Editor of the peer-reviewed academic journal:East West Journal of Humanities(EWJH). Dr. Haque completed his BA in English in 1992, and obtained his first MA in 1993 in English (Literature) from the University of Chittagong, Bangladesh. His second MA, specializing in English Language, was from University Putra Malaysia, Malaysia, in 2002. In November 2005, he completed his Ph.D. in Linguistics, specializing in Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA), from the University of Malaya, Malaysia. His passion for cinema and photography prompted him to complete his third MA, that is, MSS in Media and Communication specializing in film studies from Independent University Bangladesh in Fall-2015, as well as the yearlong Professional Programme on Photography from Pathshala, South Asian Media Institute in December 2019.Dr. Haque has presented academic papers and conducted workshops in more than 100 international and national conferences and seminars in USA, UK, Australia, Spain, Chile, China, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Bangladesh. Moreover, he has published over 30 scholarly articles in peer-reviewed journals includingMultilingua: Journal of Cross-Cultural and Interlanguage CommunicationandInternational Journal of Comic Art. Dr. Haque has also co-edited three books:Prostitution: Women, Society, State and Law(1997), published by Bangladesh National Women Lawyers’ Association (BNWLA), Dhaka, Bangladesh,Constructing Identities in the Malaysian Media(2008), by University of Malaya Press, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, andEnglish Studies and the Marketplace(2018), by East West University, Dhaka, Bangladesh. He is also producer and assistant director of the documentary filmLife after Grey(2015) (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIrqk6QWwT4&t=14s). Dr. Tanbir received Prominent Researcher Award from East West University and was honored by the Bangladesh Finance Association, University of Dhaka for his teaching and research carrier. Saiful Islam is a distinguished professor with nearly forty-three years of esteemed academic, research, and industry experience. A graduate of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET), he began his academic career at Dhaka University of Engineering and Technology (DUET) before moving to Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET). At CUET, he has held significant academic and administrative roles, including Head of the Civil Engineering Department, Dean of Engineering, Syndicate Member, and Vice-Chancellor (in charge).Prof. Saiful is a Fellow of the Institution of Engineers, Bangladesh (IEB) and brings substantial industry experience from his work with the Bureau of Research, Testing, and Consultancy (BRTC, Civil) at CUET. He has supervised eight graduate theses, including two doctoral and six M.Sc./M.Eng. theses, and has examined numerous graduate reports and theses. His scholarly contributions include more than 20 highly regarded research articles and presentations at various conferences, focusing on concrete strength, properties, and renewable materials in structural engineering.The EWU Department of Civil Engineering is honored to have Professor Dr. Md. Mobarak Hossain Khan is a Professor and the Chairperson of the Department of Social Relations at East West University (EWU), Bangladesh. Before joining at EWU on January 2018, he occupied several faculty and research positions at Bielefeld University School of Public Health (Germany), Sapporo Medical University (Japan), King Faisal University (Saudi Arabia) and Bangladesh Agricultural University and Jahangirnagar University (Bangladesh) since 1993. He finished his Habilitation (2017) in urban health from Bielefeld University, Germany; PhD (2007) in public health from Sapporo Medical University, Japan; MSc (2000) in Community Health and Health Management from Heidelberg University, Germany; MSc (1992) and BSc (1991) in Statistics from Jahangirnagar University, Bangladesh. He received various prestigious scholarships namely Monbukagakusho (Japanese government) scholarship for PhD in Japan (2002-2007), DAAD scholarship for MSc in Germany (1999-2000), University grant commission scholarship (1990) and University talent pool scholarship (1990) for securing first position in the science faculty of Jahangirnagar University. Public health especially urban health, epidemiology, biostatistics including statistical modelling, research methodology, population studies and demography are my major focuses for teaching and research. He already supervised many post-graduate theses students in Bangladesh and abroad. His total number of publications is over 130 including an edited book (2011) on urban health in megacities (Springer). He attended many international conferences and professional trainings or workshops held in China, Germany, India, Japan, Nepal, Netherlands, Portugal, Saudi Arabia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, United Kingdom and United States of America including Bangladesh. He received various research grants from various sources located in Bangladesh, Germany, and Japan. He is also strongly connected with many national and international scientists because of his long-term research/teaching records in Bangladesh and abroad.. professional experience: Professor(02.01.2018 - faculty sections academic background: Postdoctorate (University of South Africa)PhD (National Institute of Development Administration, Thailand)MA (University of York, UK)MSS (University of Dhaka)BSS (University of Dhaka). short biography: Anisur Rahman Khan is an Associate Professor in the Department of Sociology, East West University. Before joining East West University, he was a faculty member at the Bangladesh Public Administration Training Centre (BPATC). Currently, he is also holding the honorary position of Professor Extraordinarius at the Institute for Social & Health Sciences (ISHS) University of South Africa.He holds immense interest in advancing his works on rediscovering and decolonizing Bangladesh-centered sociological knowledge and realities. Currently, his academic concentration includes developing a sociology-centric knowledge base in suicide studies. He is also involved in exploring and fixing the ambivalences and vulnerabilities associated with men and masculinities in Bangladesh. In particular, he strives to bring symmetry in gender-related study, research and policy advocacy. Accordingly, his works critically reflect the need to shift the typical/linear ‘women-centric’ focus to the ‘men-inclusion’ approach.He has obtained his higher academic degrees in Dhaka, York, Bangkok and Cape Town. He has attended several professional training, workshops and conferences at home and abroad.Anisur Rahman Khan has published widely in national and international journals and contributed to several faculty sections academic background: Postdoctoralin Electrical Engineering, University of Tokyo, JapanPhDin Electrical Engineering, University of California, Riverside, USAMScin Electrical Engineering, BUET, BangladeshBScin Electrical Engineering, BUET, Bangladesh. short biography: Professor Khairul Alam received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees both in electrical engineering from Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET). He obtained a Ph.D. degree also in electrical engineering from the University of Californian, Riverside, USA. He worked with Intel at New York, USA as a summer intern. He spent two years at the University of Tokyo, Japan as a post-doctoral researcher under the JSPS fellowship of Japan government.He has been with the EEE department of East West University since January 2007. Along with teaching, he has a significant contribution in research and education. He published a book chapter, 38 journal papers, and 26 conference papers. He received the University Grants Commission award in 2009 for his research on strain effects on the performance of a graphene nanoribbon transistor.He has been serving the editor position of IEEE Transactions on Electron Devices (T-ED) since January 2019. He served the director position of institutional quality assurance cell of East West University for three years. During his period, seven departments of East West University completed the self-assessment report, external peer review, and post improvement plan. He served the external peer review team for the quality assurance of a few universities. He also served the accreditation team of BAETE for accreditation of engineering programs in Bangladesh. Naimul Haque is an Associate Professor of Civil Engineering department at the East West University, Bangladesh. He earned a B.Sc. in Civil Engineering degree from the Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET), Bangladesh and a M.Eng. in Structural Engineering and  Ph.D. in Civil Engineering from the Yokohama National University (YNU), Japan (2015). He received a number of awards for his excellent academic performance in the graduate level. Prior to joining at East West University, he worked as an Assistant Professor in Civil Engineering department at the Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET), Bangladesh. He also has professional experiences in designing civil engineering structures. Dr. Haque teaches structural analysis and design related courses in the undergraduate level. His research interests include the bridge and bluff body aerodynamics, seismic responses of civil structures and strengthening of RC building components. He published a number of research articles in international journals and conference proceedings. faculty sections academic background: Ph.D.  in Civil (Transportation) Engineering,University at Buffalo, The State University of New York, USA.M.Sc. in Civil (Transportation) Engineering,Purdue University, West Lafayette, IN, USA.B.Sc. in Civil (Transportation) Engineering, Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET).. short biography: Dr. Md Tawfiq Sarwar is an Associate Professor in the Department of Civil Engineering at East West University from May 2018.  He received his PhD fromUniversity at Buffalo, The State University of New York, USA in 2016, MSc fromPurdue University, West Lafayette, IN, USA in 2013 and BSc degree from Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) in 2009, all three in Civil Engineering with a major in Transportation Engineering.  At East West University, he is a member of the Program Self-Assessment Committee (PSAC), Department Development Committee (DDC), and the Curriculum Development and Technical Evaluation Committee.Prior to joining East West University, Dr. Sarwar served as a Research Associate for National Research Council (NRC, a sister concern of the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine,NASEM) atTurner-Fairbank Highway Research Center, Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), McLean, VA, USA.  His research interests are econometric and statistical analysis, traffic safety, planning, operation, naturalistic driving study, vulnerable road user, infrastructure and disaster management, public transportation etc.  He has worked on several projects funded by Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), National Science Foundation (NSF), Region II University Transportation Research Center (UTRC), New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Indiana Department of Transportation (INDOT) among other renowned institutes.  Using the findings of these projects, Dr. Sarwar has published several journals and conference papers (published in top-tier Elsevier/Springer journals).  Besides, he has served as a peer reviewer for several journals, such as, Accident Analysis & Prevention, Transportation Research Record, ASCE Journal of Transportation Engineering etc.. professional experience: Associate Professor,Department of Civil Engineering,East West University,Dhaka, Bangladesh. Sept 2003 - Sept. 2005. research interest: Plasma Physics:Dusty plasma physics is a specialized branch of plasma physics that focuses on plasmas containing electron, ions and charged less dust particles suspended in the ionized gas. These dust particles interact with the surrounding plasma through electrostatic forces, leading to unique behaviors and phenomena. Dusty plasmas are found in many natural environments, such as in space and  in cometary tails, and are also found in laboratory. The study of dusty plasmas provides insights into fundamental plasma dynamics, as well as practical applications in materials science, space exploration, and industrial processes involving plasma-based technologies.Cloud Electrification:Cloud electrification refers to the process by which clouds accumulate electrical charges, leading to the development of lightning and thunder. This phenomenon occurs primarily in convective clouds, such as thunderclouds, where the movement of supercooled water droplets, ice crystals, and snow particles causes collisions that transfer electrical charge. As a result, different regions of the cloud acquire positive or negative charges, creating an electric field strong enough to trigger lightning discharges, either within the cloud, between clouds, or to the ground. Understanding cloud electrification is essential for predicting and mitigating the effects of thunderstorms and lightning-related hazards.. selected publications: Journal PublicationConference & SeminarsInternational:1. Nawab Yousuf Ali completed his Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering from the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Jahangirnagar University, Dhaka, Bangladesh. He earned his M.Sc. in Computer Engineering from Lvov Polytechnic Institute, Lvov, Ukraine, USSR.He is currently serving as aProfessorin the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at East West University, Dhaka, Bangladesh, a position he has held since October 2020. Prior to this, he served in various academic and administrative capacities at East West University, including as anAssociate Professor(July 2013 - October 2020),Chairpersonof the Department of Computer Science and Engineering (August 2012 - July 2014),Assistant Professor(July 2009 - July 2013),Senior Lecturer(January 2003 - July 2009), andLecturer(January 2001 - January 2003).Dr. Md. Nawab Yousuf Ali has contributed extensively to academic research through numerous appraised papers and has showcased his work at various prestigious national and international conferences. His research articles have been published in renowned journals such as theInternational Journal of Machine Learning and Cybermetrics,MDPI-Information,International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications (IJACSA),Journal of Engineering and Applied Science,International Journal of Ambient Computing and Intelligence (IJACI),JP Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer, andInternational Journal of Artificial Life Research, among others. He has also published conference papers at globally recognized events such as IEEE AISP, ICCIT, ICSCC, ICASERT, ICSI, ICRITO, ICCCE, ICDIM, IALP and many more renowned conferences.Dr. Ali has active research collaborations with esteemed professors and researchers worldwide. His research spans diverse areas, includingNatural Language Processing,Universal Networking Language,Machine Learning,Internet of Things (IoT), andEmbedded Systems. M. A. Hakim is a Professor in the Department of Electrical & Electronic Engineering, East West University, Dhaka, Bangladesh. He received his B.Sc and M.Sc degree with distinction from Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology. He was awarded with prestigious Commonwealth Scholarship from the year 2003 to 2007 and obtained his PhD degree from the University of Southampton, UK on 2007. From 1999-2008 he worked as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Dhaka, Bangladesh and from 2007 t0 2012 he worked as a Research Scientist in Southampton Nano-Fabrication Centre, University of Southampton where he was the principal researcher & co-investigator of several UK government (EPSRC, UK) and industry funded (Sharp, OIPT, Aptamar Solutions) highly ambitious projects. He has an extensive research track record in biomedical/health technologies using heterogeneous integration of silicon nanowires & bio-nanotechnology; silicon based nano CMOS devices fabrication & characterisation; engineering of polysilicon materials for thin film transistor technology/3D integration; ZnO based nanodevices for aerospace & defence applications and classical/quantum mechanical simulation of nanodevices. In the past he invented novel methods of low temperature crystallization of amorphous silicon which have a considerable commercial potential for thin film solar cells, mass production of high quality silicon nanowires for bio-sensors & post scaling of CMOS using 3D integration. He also performed extensive research on non-classical vertical MOSFETs for a viable route for improving the RF performance of mature CMOS technologies. His group first time developed a silicidation technology for surround gate vertical MOSFETs which delivered a world record performance for Si based nMOS devices that employed only 0.5µm lithography. Most recently he led an UK Grand Challenge Project for Healthcare to develop silicon nanowire biosensors with cost-effective electronic detection, into a robust user platform for large-scale biomarker diagnostics. Dr. Hakim is currently leading research projects funded by CRT, East West University in collaboration with University of Southampton, UK for research on nanowire sensor design/sensing systems using recordReaserch projects:In Progess:Silicon nanowire biosensors for healthcare and environmental control:My current research is funded by CRT, EWU. The overall aim of this project is to perform a detail investigation of different types of silicon nanowire (SiNW) biosensors with the target to solve one of the key outstanding issues which is the determination of the required thickness, length, surface states and appropriate bias voltages of different types of nanowires for single moleculer level detection. Single crystal and polycrystalline silicon nanowires will be realized and the complicated relationship of nanowires’ electrical behavior with parameters like nanowire length, thickness, doping, bias polarity, interface states will be investigated using the industry standard Technology Computer Aided Design tool Silvaco. This project builds up a unique platform ofinternational collaboration between CRT, EWU and Southampton Nanofabrication Center, UKwhich is known as one of the topmost nanofabrication facilities in Europe. The project will have unique access to experimental samples from Southampton Nanofabrication Center, University of Southampton, UK allowing calibration, physical explanation thereby would provide the necessary insight into the required parameters for the desired electrical characteristics, process condition for realizing nanowires of appropriate materials and applicable bias conditions so that nanowire biosensor designs are optimized.Completed:Silicon nanowire arrays for viral infection markers:My most recent research project is an UK Grand Challenge Project for Healthcare engineering using heterogeneous integration of silicon nanowires & bio-nanotechnology which was honoured with £1.3 Million by Engineering & Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC), UK. This is a multidisciplinary research project in which I was a Researcher Co-investigator, Peter Ashburn as Principal Investigator and co-investigators were from the School of Medicine, Chemistry, Sociology and Electronics of the University of Southampton. The aim of this research is to develop silicon nanowire biosensors with cost-effective electronic detection, into a robust user platform for large-scale biomarker diagnostics for a personalized, proactive and preventative healthcare. I have successfully developed a generic top-down fabrication approach for polysilicon nanowire fabricatio. The polysilicon is deposited by PECVD and a special anisotropic dry etch process is used to create rectangular nanowires. The whole process does not require any expensive lithography which just uses mature microelectronics (linewidths of >3mm) and thin film technology, offering a very low cost technology. A successful integration of functional biological molecules is achieved on these nanowires and the quantification of the immobilized biological complexes is done upon application of electric field which demonstrated a commercial route for nanowire biosensor fabrication. This has created an exciting opportunity for research on low cost diagnostic platform through a second phase of grant from TSB, UK. I have actively participated on this follow up proposal preparation.Nanowires using novel materials for smart biosensors,aerospace and defence companies and photonic applications:I have also participated on a collaborative research on realising nanowires using novel materials with Prof. Peter Ashburn and Dr. Chong in Southampton which has been awarded with £360, 000 from Oxford Instrument Plasma Technology (OIPT). As a starting, remote plasma atomic layer deposition (ALD) was used to successfully grow ZnO layer with a resistivity of 1 kΩ.cm and an estimated carrier concentration of ~ 6×1019cm-3. We have extensively studied the stoichiometry of our grown ZnO layer and the quality of the layer was assessed by fabrication of staggered bottom gate thin film transistors (TFT). Recently we have successfully fabricated rectangular ZnO nanowires using my generic generic top-down fabrication approach of deposition and etch in mature microelectronics (linewidths of >3mm). Currently we are investigating the ZnO nanowires developed by the aforementioned technology and a follow up proposal is also prepared which aims to realize stable p-type ZnO layer and junction less ZnO nanowire transistors. This research has several promises for exploitation. On one side ZnO nanowires are attractive for realising smart gas sensors for healthcare & environmental control, on the other hand this research will lead to a paradigm shift in wide bandgap semiconductor devices and lead to new fields of research into zinc oxide pn diodes, photonic devices, MOSFETs, MESFETs, bipolar transistors and power devices with obvious applications in aerospace/defence companies and display companies for transparent electronics.Silicon based nano CMOS devices:I also worked on a Engineering & Physical Sciences (EPSRC), UK funded research project (£648,248) aimed at investigating non-classical vertical MOSFETs for a viable route for improving the RF performance of mature CMOS technologies which exploits the lithography independent short channel definition technique of vertical MOSFETs. Several innovations came out of this research solving the problems of overlap capacitance, short channel effects and source/drain series resistances in these devices. We are the first group to realize a silicidation technology for surround gate vertical MOSFETs which was successfully integrated with a Fillet Local Oxidation (FILOX) process. In this way, a world record fTof 20 GHz was achieved for Si based nMOS devices for 0.5µm lithography offering a low cost route for improving the RF performance of mature lateral CMOS These inventions have attracted attention of several semiconductor industries.Engineering of smart nano-materials:My PhD research was a project of SINANO which aimed to strengthen European scientific and technological excellence in the field of Si-based nanodevices. This research focused on thin layer of amorphous silicon deposition and engineering its morphology by crystallization for transistor-in-grain technology and/or large area electronics. Two novel methods of low temperature crystallization of amorphous silicon were developed during this research. One method used fluorine during metal induced lateral crystallization (MILC) of amorphous silicon which delivered dramatically increased lateral crystallization distance (65%) and a high quality silicon layer. I also identified a new amorphous silicon crystallization phenomenon which originated from the perimeter of the germanium layer during low temperature anneal and excellent grain localization was achieved without any metal contamination. The developed methods of devising poly-silicon have a considerable commercial potential for some other applications like thin film solar cells, mass production of high quality silicon nanowires for bio-sensors & obviously for post scaling of CMOS using 3D integration.Simulation & compact model development:I also got an extensive experience of process/device simulation using SILVACO & SYNOPSIS TCAD tools and Matlab, C++ environment through several simulations which I undertook in the past. Simulation of vertical MOSFETs to study the device behaviour during transition from partial to fully depleted operation in vertical MOSFETsand simulation of PIN diode fora proposed novel multiplexed near field Terahertz microscopewere carried out. A theoretical study on the quantum phenomena in deep sub micron MOSFETs with high-K dielectrics was also done. faculty sections academic background: Ph.D.in English with a secondary emphasis in Rhetoric and CompositionUniversity of Arkansas, Fayetteville, U.S.A.Dissertation Title: The Net of Nostalgia: Class, Culture, and Political Alienation and Nostalgia in Contemporary Latino and South Asian American LiteratureM Phil. in EnglishUniversity of Dhaka, BangladeshResearch Title: “Brecht in Bangladesh: The Application of His Themes and Techniques on Our Stage”M.A. in English LiteratureUniversity of Dhaka, BangladeshB.A. in EnglishUniversity of Dhaka, BangladeshHigher Secondary Certificate Examination (H.S.C.)Viqarunnisa Noon School, DhakaSecondary School Certificate Examination (S.S.C.)Viqarunnisa Noon School, Dhaka. short biography: Farzana Akhter is a Professor of English and the Dean of the Faculty of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences at East West University in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Previously, she served as the Chairperson of the Department of English. Since joining East-West University in 2000, she has taught various courses and contributed to the development of the department in multifarious ways. She is the Chief Editor of the Annual Report of EWU andVC Newsletter.After completing her BA and MA in English from the University of Dhaka, Dr. Akhter earned an MPhil from the same university. Later, she obtained her Ph.D. in English, with a secondary emphasis on Rhetoric and Composition, from the University of Arkansas in the United States. Her areas of interest include contemporary American Ethnic and Immigrant literatures, immigrant nostalgia, diaspora and belongingness, and the representation of women in the war narratives of Bangladesh.Dr. Akhter is a prolific academic writer whose work has been published in various forms such as academic papers, book chapters, encyclopedia entries, and translations. She has presented her research findings at academic conferences both nationally and internationally, in Bangladesh, the US, and Australia. Moreover, she has been invited to serve as a chair and respondent at various international conferences. Dr. Akhter has also contributed significantly in organizing a number of national and international conferences at East West University. Regarding his professional experience, he has been in teaching profession at university level over 29 years.  He has been working at East West University since 2000. Before joining East West University he worked at the Department of Management, Faculty of Business Administration, Islamic University, Kushtia for about 9 years. Professor Tanbir also served as Adjunct Professor in MBA & EMBA programs at Institute of Business Administration (IBA ) , University of Dhaka,  Independent University Bangladesh (IUB), Eastern University and Notre Dame University, Bangladesh.Professor Tanbir Ahmed Chowdhury served at East West University in different administrative positions, such as Dean of the Faculty of Business and Economics, Acting Treasurer, Chairperson of the Department of Business Administration, Coordinator of MBA & EMBA Programs and Proctor.Regarding his educational background, he pursued Ph.D in Financial Management & Quantitative techniques from University of Pune, India in 1996 under Indian Govt. Scholarships. He completed Post Graduate Fellowship under US State Govt. Fellowship from School of Education of the Pennsylvania State University, USA in 2006. He also pursued B.Com (Hons.) in Finance and M.Com in Finance & Banking from Department of Finance, University of Dhaka.About 40 of his articles have been published in different peer reviewed international & local journals. He also completed 2 Research Monographs sponsored by University Grants Commission of Bangladesh and East West University Center of Research & Training. He also participated in different international seminars/workshops as speaker of the session and session chair. Dr. Tanbir received Prominent Researcher Award from East West University and was honored by the Bangladesh Finance Association, University of Dhaka for his teaching and research carrier. Professor Tanbir also worked as an External Referee of about 30 PhD candidates of different international universities of his home country and abroad.Other than teaching, he worked as Sub- Project Manager of the project entitled “Optimizing class room learning through understanding students’ psychology”, Under Higher Education Quality Enhancement Program (HEQEP) from June 2014 to December 2016. This project was financed by the World Bank through University Grants Commission of Bangladesh (UGC) for the development of the Department of Business Administration, East West University. He is also working as a Director, Executive Development Centre (EDC), EWU, Skills for Employment Investment Opportunities Program (SEIP), Ministry of Finance, Government of Bangladesh.. professional (Hons.) in Computer Science and Engineering, Khulna University (Bangladesh). short biography: Ahmed Wasif Reza(Ph.D., M.Eng.Sc., B.Sc. Engg. (Hons.), CEng (UK)) is the Dean of the Faculty of Sciences and Engineering and a Professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) at East West University (EWU), Bangladesh. He also serves as the Additional Director, Quality Assurance, Institutional Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) at EWU. Previously, he held leadership roles as Chairperson and Acting Chairperson of the Department of CSE, as well as the Chair of the Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) Committee. His contributions to student engagement include serving as the Moderator of the EWU Robotics Club and Advisor of the IEEE Computer Society, Student Branch Chapter, EWU. Additionally, he was the Professional Activity Coordinator for the IEEE Computer Society Bangladesh Chapter in 2023. Before joining EWU, Professor Reza spent nearly eight years at the University of Malaya, Malaysia, a globally recognized institution ranked within the top 60 in the QS World Rankings. His last position there was Senior Lecturer (equivalent to Assistant Professor). He is currently the Visiting Fellow, Centre for Research in Industry 4.0 (CRI4.0), Faculty of Engineering, University of Malaya, Malaysia. Besides, he is also the Visiting Research Fellow at the School of Information Technology, Washington University of Science and Technology (WUST), Virginia, USA.  He is the Focal Person of Collaborative Research and Training Experience (CREATE) Program in Software Analytics Research (SOAR),University of Saskatchewan, Canada.Professor Reza is a recognized expert in Outcome-Based Education (OBE), accreditation, and quality assurance. He has been a key resource person and trainer for numerous workshops and seminars on OBE at East West University and other institutions in Bangladesh. He plays a vital role in academic accreditation and quality assessment as: (i) Member of the Evaluation Team (ET) for program accreditation, appointed by the Board of Accreditation for Engineering and Technical Education (BAETE), Institution of Engineers (IEB), Bangladesh. (ii) Academic Auditor, appointed by the Bangladesh Accreditation Council (BAC). (iii) Expert Member of the Quality Assurance Committee (QAC), appointed by the University Grants Commission (UGC) of Bangladesh.He has extensive experience in supervising and examining Ph.D., Master's (M.Eng.Sc. by research and M.Eng by coursework), and undergraduate students. His academic excellence has been recognized with numerous awards, including the “Excellence Award for Ph.D. Graduation on Time” and multiple “Dean’s Awards” for Teaching, as well as the “Excellence in Services Award”, all from the University of Malaya, Malaysia. With nearly two decades of academic and industrial research experience, Professor Reza has made significant contributions to fields such as: Radio Frequency Identification (RFID), Wireless Communications, Biomedical Image Processing and Bioimaging, Bioinformatics and Optimization, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Deep Learning, Robotics and the Internet of Things (IoT), Green Computing/IT and Sustainable Development, Brain-Computer Interface (BCI), Biomedical Signal Processing, and Electromagnetics.He has authored and co-authored over 375 research papers indexed in Science Citation Index (SCI)/Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus, with a citation count exceeding 3,250 (h-index: 27, i10-index: 70). His research excellence has been recognized with multiple international awards, including the "R&D Awards", "Best Researcher Award", "Outstanding Championship Award", "Excellence Contribution Award", "Excellence in Research Collaboration Award", and "Best Paper Awards" at various prestigious conferences and organizations. Professor Wasif was recognized as the "Computer Science Best Scientist in the University" and Top 3% Scientists in Computer Science among the scientists in the AD Scientific Index in 2024 and 2025. Professor Reza is a Chartered Engineer (CEng), UK, and an active professional member of IEEE and the IEEE Computer Society. He also serves as a chair, reviewer, and committee member for numerous SCI/ISI journals and conferences. His ongoing commitment to academic excellence, research, and professional engagement makes him a distinguished figure in the global scientific and engineering community.. professional experience: With a robust academic foundation, he earned his PhD in 2024 from the Bangladesh University of Professionals, focusing on the socio-cultural dynamics of lived Islam through a case study of shrines in Bangladesh. His academic journey includes an MBA in Marketing and a Master’s in Social Sciences (MSS) with First Class First honors and a gold medal from the University of Dhaka, reflecting his interdisciplinary expertise in business and social sciences. Dr. Masoom’s academic career spans over a decade, progressing from Lecturer to Associate Professor across institutions like United International University and Eastern University. His teaching roles are complemented by significant research contributions. As a Principal Investigator, he has led multiple funded projects addressing pressing social issues in Bangladesh, such as the interplay of religiosity and consumerism, gender-based marginality, and the socio-cultural determinants of health and stress. His work on “Bengali Muslim Cuisine” and “Materialistic Value-Orientation” underscores his commitment to exploring the intersection of culture, economy, and identity in contemporary Bangladeshi society.A prolific scholar, Dr. Masoom has authored over 40 academic publication with  over a dozen of Scopus-indexed publications in esteemed journals such asHeliyon,Frontiers in Psychology, andReligions, spanning topics like social capital, religiosity, perceived stress, and educational challenges. His research often bridges sociology with organizational psychology and business studies, offering nuanced insights into urbanization, gender dynamics, and religious practices. He also serves as a Review Editor forFrontiers in Psychology, contributing to academic peer-review processes.  Recognized for his scholarly excellence, He received the UGC Research Support Fund for his PhD dissertation and the Nazmul Karim Memorial Gold Medal for academic distinction. His administrative roles include a decade-long tenure as Assistant Proctor at United International University, highlighting his leadership in academia. Dr. Masoom leverages advanced statistical tools like SPSS and AMOS in his research. Beyond academia, he moderates debating clubs, fostering intellectual discourse among students.  Born in 1980, he resides in Dhaka with his family. faculty sections academic background: Ph.D in Applied Mathematics, Tokyo Institute of Technology (TIT), Japan. short biography: Md. Fazlul Karimis a Professor ofMathematics in the Department of Mathematical and Physical Sciences, East West University, Bangladesh, where he has been since 2018. He was first appointed as an Associate Professor and later on promoted to Professor. During 2010-2017, he was a Principal Lecturer at University Technology Brunei (UTB), Brunei Darussalam. He has also worked at University Science Malaysia (USM), University of Dhaka and Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, Sylhet.He received his BSc (Honours) and MSc in Mathematics from the Department of Mathematics, Jahangirnagar University, Bangladesh.In 1996, he was awarded the Monbusho Scholarship for doing PhD in Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) in the Department of Mechano Aerospace Engineering, Tokyo Institute of Technology (TIT), Japan and successfully awarded PhD in March 2000.His research interests are: Turbulent flow using Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS), Mathematical Modelling of Long Wave (Tsunami and Storm Surge), Heat and Mass transfer. He has developed mathematical models to simulate Tsunami and Storm Surge. He has over 60 peer-reviewed international journal publications and over 21 international conference papers. The findings reveal that precipitation significantly increases crash risk, with an annual minimum rise of 32% and an average increase of 38%. Interestingly, rainy conditions are associated with reduced crash severity compared to dry weather. Although the relative risk is higher for all crash types during rainy conditions, the relative risk for no-injury crashes is 40% higher compared to fatal crashes (< 1% of all crashes). Spatial analysis highlights a correlation between population density and crash frequency. Moreover, the study investigates the interplay among roadway types, weather conditions, and driver behavior. Precipitation intensity was associated with a 36–52% increase in crash risk, with higher increases for more intense rainfall (over 25 mm/hr). The relative risk varied by age group. The highest risk was observed in young adults (18–30 years old) and the lowest in individuals older than 65. Generally, females exhibited a risk that was 7–13% lower than their male counterpart, depending on the age group. Temporal factors—including time of day, day of the week, and month of the year—significantly impact road safety during precipitation, with early morning hours posing the highest crash risk due to rush hour traffic and changing lighting conditions. This comprehensive study enhances our understanding of road safety dynamics, providing foundational insights to inform policy development for safer and more sustainable transportation systems. Addressing human factors, alongside advancements in vehicle safety technology and road design, holds promise for reducing crash severity and improving overall road safety outcomes.. awards and achievement: CoE Scholarship, UTSA (2016-2018)Academic Excellence Scholarship, UTSA (2018-2021)Ex-National Champion in Table Tennis, Bangladesh (Junior and Sub-Junior Level). awards honors: Awards And Achievement. teaching materials: Dr. Billah has been working as a teacher of the following subjects:CE100: Civil Engineering DrawingCE103: Surveying and Introduction to GISCE200: Details of ConstructionCE208/408: Quantity Surveying and Cost AnalysisCE261: Fluid MechanicsCE361/CE461: Open Channel FlowCE463: Hydrology, Irrigation, and Flood ControlCE498: Thesis/Project. affiliation professional membership: Member, Institute of Engineers Bangladesh

faculty sections academic background: Ph.D. in Photonics, City University, London, UK.Master’s in Electrical Engineering, University of Alabama, USA.B.Sc in Electrical & Electronic Engineering, Bangladesh Institute of Technology (BIT Chittagong) (at present CUET). short biography: Dr. Mohammed Moseeur Rahman received his B.Sc. (Eng.) degree in the year 1997 from Bangladesh Institute of Technology, Chittagong with distinction. At present it is known as CUET. He was awarded Institute Gold Medal for securing the highest percentage of marks among all the recipients of Bachelor's degree in the passing session. He earned his M.Sc. (Eng.) degree in the year 2001 from the University of Alabama, USA, with CGPA 4.00 (out of 4.00). His master's research concentrated on hetero-associative pattern recognition, where he proposed a filter to detect and locate dissimilar group targets from given test images. It was published in a reputed journal. He has served as an assistant professor in two reputed private universities in Bangladesh for more than nine years. Later he obtained his Ph.D. in photonics from City University London, UK, in the year 2016. His doctoral research was regarding finite-element based numerical analysis of sound and light interactions in optical waveguides. His work was published in couple of journals and as a book chapter. When he was doctoral student, he served as visiting lecturer in the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering at City University, London. He also served as Post Doctoral Research Assistant in the Photonics Modelling Group under the Research Centre for Photonics and Instrumentation, City, University of London. faculty sections academic background: PhD in English Literature, University of Bamberg, GermanyEuropean Joint Master’s Degree in English and American Studies, University of Bamberg, GermanyMA in English, Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, BangladeshBA (Hons) in English, Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, Bangladesh. short biography: Dr. Md Abu Shahid Abdullahcompleted his MA in English and American Studies and his PhD in English literature at Otto-Friedrich University Bamberg, Germany. He is currently an Associate Professor in English at East West University, Bangladesh. His research interests include trauma, alienation, memory, identity, marginalisation and magical realism. He has published book chapters with publishing houses like Palgrave Macmillan and Cambridge Scholars Publishing and over 20 articles in different international journals. He has also presented over 50 research papers at different international conferences. His first bookTraumatic Experience and Repressed Memory in Magical Realist Novels: Speaking the Unspeakableand his second bookTrauma, Memory and Identity Crisis: Reimagining and Rewriting the Pastwas published by Cambridge Scholars Publishing, UK in 2020 and 2022 respectively. His third bookMagical Feminism in the Americas: Resisting Female Marginalisation and Oppression through Magic,was published by Vernon Press, USA in 2024. Born in 1977, she developed an early interest in the field of pharmacy, driven by a desire to make a meaningful impact on patient well-being.Ms. Farhana earned her Bachelor of Pharmacy (B. PHRM) degree with honors from the first private University of Medicine and Pharmacy of Bangladesh, University of Science & Technology, Chittagong (USTC). Recognized for her academic excellence, she continued her education, completing a Master's in Pharmaceutical Sciences, focusing on general pharmacy. After completing her M. PHRM, Ms. Rizwan transitioned to academia, joining the faculty at a renowned private university, East West University. Her teaching philosophy revolves around nurturing a deep understanding of pharmaceutical principles while inspiring critical thinking among her students. Known for her engaging lectures and commitment to mentorship, she has played a pivotal role in shaping the next generation of pharmacists.Driven by a commitment to scholarly pursuits, Farhana pursued a Ph.D. in Clinical Pharmacy & Pharmacology from Jadavpur University, Kolkata, a leading research institution of India. Her doctoral research delved into pre-clinical and clinical research, contributing valuable insights to the field. During this time, she published several peer-reviewed articles in reputable scientific journals, establishing herself as a rising star in clinical research.Simultaneously, Dr. Rizwan continued her research endeavors, securing research grants and collaborating with industry partners. Currently, a collaborative research project is going on, titled, “Lipid Nano capsule loaded topical system for transdermal delivery of estradiol as hormone replacement therapy for early postmenopausal women”, funded by Beximco Pharmaceuticals Limited. Her work has spanned a diverse range of topics, from nanoparticle based-drug discovery to analytical pharmaceutical chemistry, demonstrating her versatility in contributing to various aspects of pharmaceutical science. Her commitment to the advancement of pharmaceutical knowledge and dedication to improving patient outcomes exemplify her as a leader in the field.Beyond her academic and research pursuits, Farhana remains actively involved in various departmental activities, contributing to Department Development Committee, Technical Committee, Curriculum Development Committee, Examination Committee, Ethical Review Committee of Pharmacy department of EWU, and advocating for advancements in pharmacy practice. faculty sections academic background: Postdoctoral Fellow (Fulbright Visiting Scholar 2024-25), Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences, College of Pharmacy, Mercer University, Atlanta, Georgia, USAPhD in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Jahangirnagar University in collaboration with Bangladesh Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (BCSIR), Dhaka, BangladeshMS in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Department of Pharmacy, Jahangirnagar University, Savar, Dhaka, Bangladesh.Bachelor of Pharmacy , Jahangirnagar University, Savar, Dhaka, Bangladesh.. short biography: Dr. Nazia Hoque is a dedicated academic and researcher with over 16 years of teaching experience at several reputed universities in Bangladesh. She currently serves as an Associate Professor in the Department of Pharmacy at East West University, Dhaka, where she continues to inspire and mentor future pharmaceutical scientists. Dr. Hoque earned her B. Pharm and M.S. in Pharmaceutical Sciences from the Department of Pharmacy, Jahangirnagar University, Dhaka, Bangladesh. She later obtained her Ph.D. in Pharmaceutical Sciences from the same institution, in collaboration with the Bangladesh Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (BCSIR), Dhaka. In recognition of her academic excellence, she was awarded the prestigiousFulbright Visiting Scholar Postdoctoral Fellowship (2024–25), administered by the U.S. Department of State’s Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs. During her postdoctoral research at the Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences, College of Pharmacy, Mercer University, Georgia, USA, she investigated the role of bioactive molecules in inhibiting vascular inflammation and hypertension, contributing to the prevention of cardiovascular diseases.Dr. Hoque’s primary research interests lie in cardiovascular pharmacology, particularly in exploring how naturally occurring microbial metabolites modulate vascular inflammation and endothelial activation, with the goal of identifying novel therapeutic strategies for inflammatory cardiovascular diseases. In addition, her research encompasses the medicinal plants of Bangladesh and their associated endophytic fungi, focusing on their antioxidant, cytotoxic, antimicrobial, antidiabetic, antinociceptive, and anti-inflammatory activities. She is particularly interested in the isolation and characterization of bioactive compounds from endophytic fungi and medicinal plants, highlighting their potential as novel drug candidates. Her research findings have been published in several reputed national and international peer-reviewed journals and conference proceedings. She has presented her work at numerous scientific conferences worldwide, earning distinguished recognition, including the ‘Young Ethnopharmacologist Award’ for Best Oral Presentation at the 18th International Congress of the International Society for Ethnopharmacology, Dhaka. She was awarded 1st place in the Oral Presentation category at the 2025 Mercer School of Medicine–College of Pharmacy (SOM–COP) Joint Research Conference, Atlanta, USA—an achievement that underscores the strength of her international scientific collaborations.Dr. Hoque currently serves as the Principal Investigator (PI) of a research project funded by the Center for Research and Training (CRT), East West University. faculty sections academic background: 2023_Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D) in Civil Engineering (Environmental Engineering), Sultan Qaboos University, Sultanate of Oman.2017_Masters of Science (M.Sc) in Civil Engineering (Environmental Engineering), Islamic University of Technology (IUT-OIC), Bangladesh.2012_Bachelor of Science (B.Sc) in Civil Engineering, Islamic University of Technology (IUT-OIC), Bangladesh.. short biography: Dr. Sadik Rahman is a passionate young environmental researcher with nearly four years of full-time university teaching experience and 1.5 years in the industry. He holds a B.Sc. and M.Sc. in Civil Engineering from the Islamic University of Technology (IUT), with a focus on water quality monitoring and remediation. Dr. Rahman has worked in notable research initiatives, including a WHO water quality monitoring project and environmental strategic projects for the Sultanate of Oman.During his doctoral studies, Dr. Rahman researched innovative and promising bio-electrochemical wastewater treatment and desalination processes, which investigated nanomaterial application to enhance desalination performance. Alongside, he also worked on projects related to anaerobic digestion, waste-to-resource recovery, and the application of AI in environmental remediation. With over five years of expertise in bio-electrochemical systems, he has excelled in system design, reactor fabrication, operation, and optimization, complemented by more than three years of experience in drinking water quality research. He led a prize-winning project to developa mobile application for real-time solid waste collection and notification for Oman Environmental Services Holding Company—be'ah. His publication in high-impact journals attracted more than three international and prestigious recognitions awarded by the Ministry of Higher Education, Research, and Innovation in the years 2020, 2022, and 2023. His intriguing postgraduate project to use petrochemical wastewater to produce electricity for desalination was awarded by the Gulf Petrochemical and Chemicals Association (GPCA) in 2022.Dr. Rahman has 17 peer-reviewed publications in high-impact journals, notably in theJournal of Cleaner Production(Q1, 9.8),Desalination(Q1, 8.4),Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews(Q1, 16.3),Materials Today Sustainability(Q1, 7.1),Science of the Total Environment(Q1, 8.2),Environmental Research(Q1, 7.7), etc. He has presented his work at numerous conferences. He has supervised four undergraduate research groups and mentored three graduate students. Research outcomes of Dr. Rahman received international recognition for his contributions to research excellence and innovation, including a best doctoral thesis award. His work has received nearly 440 citations on Google Scholar (h-index: 11, i10-index: 11) and a ResearchGate score exceeding 310. Dr. Rahman is very keen to collaborate on industry-driven, cross-disciplinary challenges in environmental engineering and sustainable development.During his tenure as a faculty member, Dr. Rahman was involved in several administrative andcommitteeduties for departmental improvement. He is actively involved in the outcome-based education (OBE) process in East West University for theWASHINGTON ACCORDaccreditation byBAETE. She started her carrier in 2004 as Medical Officer in clinical medicine in the department of pediatrics. Then she joined 25thBCS in 2006 but left after a year due to her son’s health issues. In 2008, she started her journey in public health and joined NGO Forum for Public Health and visited many arsenic affected areas of the country for mitigation purpose. She completed her MPH in Epidemiology in 2011 from State University of Bangladesh (SUB) and started her research carrier in ICDDRB, where she was involved with a cohort study and a clinical trial on maternal and child health. From here she developed her research interest in sexual reproductive health, maternal and child health, adolescent health and related public health issues. She joined East West University in 2013 as Lecturer and started taking courses on reproductive health, adolescent and development, public health, epidemiology, STD and HIV/AIDS, genetics etc. In 2017, she completed her MPhil in Preventive and Social Medicine from National Institute of Preventive and Social Medicine (NIPSOM) under Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University (BSMMU) and got promoted as Senior Lecturer. She has a number of journal article publications in national and  international journals and few conference papers. With her colleagues she has completed a research project funded by EWUCRT and submitted another research proposal recently. Bachelor of Social Sciences (BSS) in Sociology, University of Dhaka, Bangladesh. short biography: Dr. Rasel Hussain is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Sociology and.Assistant Proctor at East West University  He completed his Doctor of Philosophy (DPhil) from the Department of Sociology and Social Policy of Lingnan University, Hong Kong with the prestigious HKPFS Scholarship by RGC of Hong Kong. Earlier he worked as a Consultant of REACH, University of Oxford and Coventry University, the United Kingdom. Dr. Hussain has been awarded the prestigious “Young Researcher of the Year” at the International Educational Awards – LEAP (Leadership in Education, Advancement, and Progress) 2025, hosted by the London School of Digital Business. He recently completed a funded project with National Institute of Local Government (NILG), Bangladesh Government and also working now with BPATC and EWUCRT funded research Project. Very recently he has been awarded as the best researcher in the rank of Assistant Professor at the Faculty of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences (FLASS) of East West University. His research interest and academic publications fall in the areas of urban economy, informal economy, information-based economy, urban marginality, environmental crises, poverty, gender studies, gerontology and so on. He also worked as a Founding Moderator of the East West University Sociology Club. He teaches at Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT) and Asian University Bangladesh (AUB) as a faculty of Sociology.He developed his expertise  in the field of Urban Sociology, Demography, Gender studies, and Gerontology. His research interest falls in the arenas of Urban Economy, Informal economy, information based economy and urban marginality, Poverty and Gender studies, Gerontology and so on. He had handful of experiences about field research in connection with different INGO’s and NGO’s including icddr,b, UNICEF, Save the Children, Nielsen, Plan International, Ministry of Health, University Grant Commission(UGC), Bangladesh Medical Research Council(BMRC) and so on at home and abroad and thus gathered handful experience in both quantitative and qualitative research.Mr. Hussain is publishing and presenting his research articles from the reputed journal and conferences at home and abroad with the progress of his academic journey. Currently, he is doing his research on information based economy, Masculinity and suicide in the context of South Asian Societies.
