miscellaneous type: policy. description: ELECTIVE_OTHER_MAJORS: In addition to completing 13 courses of one of three major streams, each student has to take 6 elective courses from other two major streams. For example, if a student aims to get specialization in the Public Health Stream, he/she will take six elective courses from the remaining 26 courses mentioned in Population Sciences and Environmental Health streams. Similarly, students aiming to get major in Population Sciences will take 6 courses from Public Health and Environmental Health streams. These courses are much more relevant for the PPHS program than optional courses. These courses will be offered in the 3rd and 4th year of the program.

miscellaneous type: admission_requirements. description: Minimum qualifications for admission to the Bachelor program are as follows: 1. Minimum GPA of 3.00 in both SSC and HSC Examinations or 2. Candidates must have passed University of London and Cambridge GCE ‘O’ Level in at least five subjects and ‘A’ Level in at least two subjects. Only the best five subjects in ‘O’ Level and best two subjects in ‘A’ Level will be considered. Out of these seven subjects, a candidate must have at least 4B’s or GPA of 4.00 in the four subjects and 3 C’s or GPA of 3.5 in the remaining three subjects. (in the scale of A=5, B=4, C=3, D=2 and E=1 or 3. American High School Diploma; and 4. Acceptable EWU Admission Test Score. 5. Total GPA of 5.00 in both SSC and HSC Examinations for the children of Freedom Fighter. 6. The final selection of candidates for admission in the Bachelor Programs at EWU will be based on the Admission Test scores obtained with 75% from admission test, 10% from SSC/O-level and 15% from HSC/A-level. Foreign students fulfilling EWU admission eligibility may not need to appear at the Admission Test. However, an equivalence committee will assess and recommend for satisfactory grade for the applicants who seek admission in EWU. A committee will assess and recommend for waiver of Admission Test, Scholarship etc. (if applicable) for foreign students and the students from other systems.

policies principles name: Energy Use Efficiency. details: Achieve energy efficiency by mitigating waste and switching to alternative technology, which includes converting all lighting to energy-saving devices with sensory panels, installing solar panels, and ensuring all new construction maximizes natural lighting and utilizes energy-saving devices.

policies principles name: Water Use Efficiency. details: Minimize water consumption and maximize recycling/reuse of water resources through strategies like installing automated sensory water dispensers, regularly monitoring for zero leakage, recycling all wastewater for gardening, and ensuring new construction includes provision for rainwater harvesting.

policies principles name: Paper Use Reduction. details: Minimize paper usage by reducing reliance on printed material, adopting a Learning Management System (LMS) for classes, discouraging unnecessary printing, adopting ERP systems to streamline operations, and creating archives for thesis work.

policies principles name: Responsible Waste Management. details: Manage and process all university waste according to health and environmental practices. This involves installing color-coded bins, sorting and processing all recyclable waste (especially paper), installing a Sewage Treatment Plant, and ensuring proper disposal of all hazardous waste.

policies principles name: Alignment with Climate Action Goals. details: The procurement process is designed to align with the university's climate action goals by prioritizing environmentally sustainable and ethically sourced products and services.

policies principles name: Favoring Sustainable Suppliers. details: The policy shall favor suppliers and vendors that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability, such as those offering energy-efficient equipment, renewable materials, and products with minimal environmental impact.
policies principles name: Promoting Local Sourcing. details: The policy encourages the purchase of locally sourced goods to reduce transportation emissions and support local economies.

policies principles name: Waste Reduction in Procurement. details: Emphasis is placed on reducing waste by selecting products with minimal packaging and promoting the use of reusable or recyclable materials.

policies principles name: ESG and Ethical Standards Alignment. details: Ensure that all investment operations reflect East West University's ethical standards and its commitment to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues.

policies principles name: Long-Term Sustainable Return. details: Ensure a successful long-term investment return and guarantee a better return at a lower risk through sustainable investment practices.

policies principles name: Screening for Societal Harm. details: Apply a combination of negative and positive screens to exclude companies that may be harmful to society and/or the environment and to invest in businesses with good governance.
policies principles name: Contribution to SDGs. details: Embrace the university's unique role in contributing to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

policies principles name: Non-Discrimination and Anti-Harassment. details: Enforce zero tolerance for any acts of discrimination, harassment, or inequity [cite: 21][cite_start], and implement policies conforming to national legislation and international standards on human rights[cite: 22].

policies principles name: Inclusive Recruitment and Retention. details: Actively recruit and retain diverse talents across faculty, staff, and students [cite: 24][cite_start], while ensuring equitable access to professional development and leadership opportunities[cite: 25].

policies principles name: Accessible Learning and Working Environments. details: Ensure physical and digital accessibility for all, including those with special needs [cite: 27][cite_start], offer necessary accommodations [cite: 28][cite_start], and provide supportive facilities for women, such as daycare, a maternity leave policy, and specialized accommodation/transportation[cite: 30, 31].

policies principles name: Education and Awareness. details: Integrate EDI concepts into curriculum, research, and training [cite: 33][cite_start], and organize workshops, seminars, and campaigns for awareness and sensitization on EDI issues[cite: 34, 40].

policies principles name: Zero-Tolerance Policy and Integrity. details: East West University (EWU) upholds a zero-tolerance approach to bribery and corruption, committing to conducting all operations ethically, transparently, and in compliance with all relevant anti-corruption laws.

policies principles name: Absolute Prohibition of Bribery and Corruption. details: The university prohibits any form of direct or indirect bribery (offering, giving, receiving, or soliciting anything of value to influence actions) and corrupt practices (abuse of power, fraud, embezzlement, or misuse of authority). This includes prohibiting the giving of undue academic advantage to any student.

policies principles name: Prohibition of Facilitation Payments. details: EWU strictly prohibits the offering, making, demanding, or accepting of any form of facilitation payment, as these are considered illegal forms of bribery, with no exceptions, even if they are customary in certain contexts.

policies principles name: Strict Rules on Gifts and Hospitality. details: Gifts, hospitality, or donations are prohibited if they are lavish, offered with the expectation of a business advantage, or given during negotiations/tenders. Acceptable practices require all gifts to be reasonable, proportionate, and properly documented for transparency.

policies principles name: Meaningful Partnerships and Community Improvement. details: The policy is designed to promote meaningful partnerships between EWU students and diverse communities (including government and non-governmental organizations), enriching student experiences while nurturing goodwill, driving community improvement, and creating sustainable benefits for all involved.

policies principles name: Raising Community Service Awareness and Connectivity. details: To raise the level of awareness and interest in community service programs for all students through active and regular engagements, which strengthens connectivity among the university, its students, and the community.

policies principles name: Socio-Cultural Understanding and Sustainable Society. details: To establish community bonding that helps students empathize with others, appreciate diversity, improve their understanding of the socio-cultural context, and acquire practical knowledge, ultimately contributing to building a more sustainable society.

policies principles name: Skill Development and Future Opportunities. details: To help students connect with fellow volunteers, mentors, professionals, and community leaders for guidance and opportunities, enabling them to gain knowledge and develop self-confidence and self-esteem to thrive in complex societal challenges.

policies principles name: Culture Development and Responsibility. details: Develop a culture of environmental and social responsibility within the university community and promote student, faculty, and staff engagement in social and environmental initiatives.

policies principles name: Skill Acquisition and Practical Knowledge. details: Equip students with practical knowledge and skills in sustainable development and social welfare, ensuring they are prepared to address real-world social and environmental challenges.

policies principles name: Academic and Co-Curricular Integration. details: Integrate social and environmental aspects into academic curricula, research, and extracurricular activities to align with global Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

policies principles name: Reputation and Global Citizenship. details: Enhance global reputation and ranking through active participation in SDG-related metrics and community impact projects, reflecting the university's commitment to global citizenship.

policies principles name: Policy Goals and Academic Integrity. details: The Disciplinary Policy is aimed at upholding the name and reputation of the University, maintaining order, discipline, safety, and security, and ensuring the integrity and quality of all academic and assessment processes at the University.

policies principles name: General Conduct and Duty. details: Every member must conform to and abide by all rules, observe and obey all orders and directions from the University, discharge their assigned duties faithfully, honestly, and diligently, and use their utmost endeavors to promote the interests of the University.

policies principles name: Professional Decorum and Secrecy. details: Members must observe proper decorum and show courtesy in all matters. They must also maintain strict secrecy regarding the affairs of the University and not divulge the contents of any document, except to their section head, the Vice Chancellor, and persons involved in processing the document.

policies principles name: Upholding Academic Integrity. details: East West University is committed to upholding the highest standards of academic integrity and honesty. Plagiarism is defined as using another person's ideas, words, or work without properly acknowledging the source.

policies principles name: Comprehensive Definition of Plagiarism. details: Plagiarism includes, but is not limited to, reproducing lecture notes or copying/pasting text without citation, fabricating or using incorrect references, using figures, codes, or images without acknowledgment, using phrases without quotation marks, paraphrasing without proper attribution, and submitting someone else's work as one's own.

policies principles name: Universal Scope and Application. details: This policy applies to all University community members, including undergraduate and postgraduate students, faculty, researchers, and staff. It covers all academic submissions such as assignments, research papers, theses, dissertations, publications, projects, and creative compositions.

policies principles name: Ethical, Transparent, and Compliant Use. details: East West University (EWU) encourages ethical, innovative, and productive use of AI tools, while strictly considering misuse and abuse of AI tools as a punishable offense. All activities must be ethical, transparent, and in compliance with all related legal and societal norms, policies, and laws.

policies principles name: Academic Integrity and Citation Mandate. details: The policy requires proper citation and permission for all permitted AI-generated content. A maximum of one percent of raw GenAI-generated sentences or two percent of sentences rephrased using a second GenAI tool may be used in any report or publication, with full disclosure of the tools and dates used.

policies principles name: Prohibition of Deception and Harmful Content. details: Strictly prohibits using AI tools for impersonation, completing assignments without explicit permission from the supervisor, generating misinformation or unethical elements, and creating content subversive to the interests of any person, community, society, nation, politics, culture, religion, or public health.

policies principles name: Intellectual Property and Legal Compliance. details: Users must not violate intellectual property laws or any related national and international laws when using AI tools. AI research and tools development must be guided by national and international norms, conventions, and laws.
policies principles name: Carbon Footprint Reduction. details: To reduce the university's carbon footprint through energy-efficient and sustainable practices.
policies principles name: Renewable Energy Adoption. details: To promote the adoption of renewable energy sources, such as solar or wind power.
policies principles name: Integration of Sustainability. details: To integrate sustainability principles into academic curricula and research initiatives.
policies principles name: Stakeholder Engagement. details: To actively engage students, faculty, and staff in climate action programs.

policies principles name: Compliance and Monitoring. details: To ensure compliance with national and international environmental standards and establish a comprehensive monitoring and reporting framework for carbon emissions.

policies evaluation_rules name: CGPA Calculation. details: CGPA is calculated by dividing total grade points by credits attempted (A+ through F). For repeated courses, only the grade from the last attempt is used.

policies evaluation_rules name: Re-Scrutiny of Scripts. details: Re-evaluation is not allowed; only Re-Scrutiny for marking errors is permitted. A Tk.200 fee per script is charged, refunded if the faculty member is at fault.

policies evaluation_rules name: Undergraduate Probation and Dismissal. details: UG students with CGPA 1.0-2.25 are on probation for two semesters. Failure to reach 2.25 results in dismissal. CGPA below 1.0 is automatic dismissal. Failing remedial courses twice also leads to probation. Dismissed students can seek readmission to another program via the Admission Test.

policies evaluation_rules name: Graduate Probation and Dismissal. details: Graduate students with CGPA below 2.60 are on probation for a maximum of two consecutive semesters. Failure to raise CGPA to 2.60 or above results in dismissal.

policies evaluation_rules name: Incomplete (I) Grade. details: An 'I' grade is for students who completed all requirements except the final exam. If not completed within one week of the next semester, the 'I' automatically converts to an 'F'.
policies evaluation_rules name: Withdrawal (W) Grade. details: The 'W' grade is assigned for officially dropping a course within the Academic Calendar's specified date.

policies evaluation_rules name: Course Retake Policy. details: Passing grades can be retaken only once. 'F' grades can be retaken multiple times; previous 'F' becomes 'R', and the last attempt counts in CGPA. Written permission, re-registration, and fees are required. Students using this policy are ineligible for Gold Medal/Distinction.

policies evaluation_rules name: Academic Honesty and Cheating. details: The university has zero-tolerance for cheating (copying, unfair means). Disciplinary action follows. Faculty must prevent/detect cheating and report any student found cheating to the Dean.

policies evaluation_rules name: Leave of Absence and Unauthorized Absence. details: Leave (up to 3 consecutive semesters/1 year) is for students in good standing (UG: 2.25+, Grad: 2.60+). Dean grants leave. **Probationary Leave:** Possible for the 2nd semester of probation on compassionate grounds after completing the 1st. **Unauthorized Absence:** Penalties (20%-40% of 9 credits tuition) apply based on duration (1-3 semesters). Exceeding 3 semesters results in 'Officially Withdrawn' status. New students can defer the first semester for a Tk.3,000 fee.
